Mithridates VI Eupator: King of Pontus from 120 to 63 BC.
This 14th-century Ottoman sultan conquered Adrianople and made it his new capital, then forced the rulers of Serbia, Bulgaria, and Byzantium to pay him tribute — who was he?
Murad I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1362 to 1389.
Launched in 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman, this Saudi megaproject at the northern tip of the Red Sea was eventually scaled way back amid delays, cost overruns, and criticism — what is it?
Neom: Planned city in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed the 'Demon King of the Sixth Heaven,' this 16th-century samurai is regarded as the first of Japan's three great unifiers, paving the way for retainers Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu — who is he?
Oda Nobunaga: Japanese samurai and warlord (1534–1582)

First championed at an 1900 conference organized by a Trinidadian barrister to protest colonial land theft, this movement seeks unity among indigenous peoples and diaspora descendants of one continent — which movement?
Pan-Africanism: Movement encouraging solidarity among people of African ancestry.

An oligarch who once headed Ukraine's National Bank council, he won the presidency in a 2014 landslide with over 55% in the first round and led the country through the early war in Donbas — who is he?
Petro Poroshenko: President of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019.
Born into the Greek and Danish royal families and exiled as a toddler, he became Britain's longest-serving royal consort after beginning to write to a 13-year-old princess in 1939 — who is he?
Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh: Consort of Elizabeth II from 1952 to 2021.
He became Britain's first Labour prime minister in 1924, then was expelled from his own party in 1931 for leading a Conservative-dominated National Government — who was he?
Ramsay MacDonald: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1924; 1929–1935)
The first person to navigate the Northwest Passage by sea, this Norwegian explorer later led the first party to reach the South Pole aboard the ship Fram — who is he?
Wounded five times in the Civil War — most seriously at South Mountain — this staunch abolitionist and brevet major general went on to become the 19th president; who was he?
Rutherford B. Hayes: President of the United States from 1877 to 1881.
Renowned in the Book of Genesis for her hospitality and beauty, this matriarch was the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac — who is she?
Sarah: Biblical matriarch. Sarah (originally Sarai) is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions.
Pitting Britain and Prussia against France and Austria from 1756 to 1763, this global conflict was later dubbed the 'First World War' by Winston Churchill for its sheer scale — what was it called?
Seven Years' War: Global war among European powers (1756–1763)
Born into a wealthy Caracas family and nicknamed El Libertador, this military officer led six present-day South American nations to independence from Spain — who was he?
Simón Bolívar: Venezuelan statesman and military officer (1783–1830)
After running for president as the 1948 Dixiecrat candidate, this South Carolina senator served 47 years and switched from Democrat to Republican in 1964 — who was he?
This 18th-century French showman and soldier could swallow corks, stones, and live animals, and was constantly ravenous no matter how much he ate — who was he?
Tarrare: French showman and voracious eater (c. 1772–1798)
Called the "father of mindfulness," this Vietnamese Zen monk founded the Plum Village Tradition and was exiled in 1966 for opposing the war and refusing to take sides — who was he?
Thích Nhất Hạnh: Vietnamese Buddhist monk and activist (1926–2022)
The second Rashidun caliph and a father-in-law of the prophet Muhammad, he once set out to kill Muhammad with his sword before a spiritual break led him to convert in 616 — who was he?
While imprisoned at Ratnagiri in 1923, this Indian politician coined the Hindu-nationalist ideology of Hindutva and had earlier co-founded a secret society called Abhinav Bharat — who was he?
Vinayak Damodar Savarkar: Indian politician and ideologue (1883–1966)

Named after the city where its constitution was drafted, this German state of 1918 to 1933 marked the country's first constitutional experiment of its kind — a label later coined by Hitler in 1929 — what was it called?
Weimar Republic: German state from 1918 to 1933. The state was officially named the German Reich; but was more commonly referred to, and unofficially proclaimed itself, as the German Republic.
An assistant marshal to his brother Virgil, this lawman is famously credited as the key figure in the 1881 gunfight at the O.K. Corral — who is he?

This Polish politician served two stints as justice minister — one ending under PM Mateusz Morawiecki in 2023 — while also holding the prosecutor general post and championing an anti-corruption crusade — who is he?
Who among these was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Anna Atkins (born 1799) is the earliest of the four. Anna Atkins (née Children; 16 March 1799 – 9 June 1871) was an English botanist and photographer.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below was established earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
John Tyndall is a physicist. John Tyndall (2 August 1820 – 4 December 1893) was an Irish physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Fritz Haber is a chemist. For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
What is the atomic number of Aluminium?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
In what year was Pavel Durov born?
Pavel Durov: Pavel Valeryevich Durov (Russian: Павел Валерьевич Дуров; born 10 October 1984) is a technology entrepreneur.
In what year was Alexander Fleming born?
Alexander Fleming: Sir Alexander Fleming (6 August 1881 – 11 March 1955) was a Scottish physician and microbiologist.
In what year was Satya Nadella born?
Satya Nadella: Satya Narayana Nadella (born 19 August 1967) is an Indian-American business executive.
In what year did Sergei Korolev die?
Sergei Korolev: Originally trained as an aircraft designer, Korolev became a leading figure in Soviet rocketry.
In what year did Max Born die?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Bayes' theorem discovered?
Bayes' theorem: The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.
Genetics: Gregor Mendel. Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Doxycycline: Pfizer. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
In which country is St. Bernard?

St. Bernard (dog breed): Switzerland. The hospice, built by and named after the Alpine monk Saint Bernard of Menthon, 
acquired its first dogs between 1660 and 1670.
Who is credited with discovering General relativity?
General relativity: Albert Einstein. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Who is credited with discovering Tetracycline?
Tetracycline: Lloyd Conover. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Who is credited with discovering Potassium?
Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
NATO codenamed 'Curl' and nicknamed 'Nastia' in the USSR, this twin-engine turboprop transport was later license-built in China as the Xi'an Y-7 — what is it?

Antonov An-26 (NATO reporting name: Curl, nicknamed Nastia in the USSR) is a twin-engined turboprop regional airliner and military transport aircraft, designed and produced in the Soviet Union from 1969 to 1986.
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Biceps is a large muscle that lies on the front of the upper arm between the shoulder and the elbow.

Derived from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart', this medical term describes a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes a red flag, sometimes just a sign of a well-conditioned athlete. Name the condition?
Bradycardia (brads), meaning "slow", and (karda), meaning "heart", also called bradyarrhythmia, is a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute (BPM).
This opportunistic yeast lives harmlessly in the gut and mouth of most healthy adults, but can turn pathogenic in immunocompromised people, causing a common fungal infection — what species is it?
Candida albicans is an opportunistic pathogenic yeast that is a common member of the human gut flora.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.
Released on a daily cycle and spiking when you're stressed, this glucocorticoid raises blood sugar through gluconeogenesis and even tamps down the immune system — what stress hormone is it?
Cortisol is a steroid hormone in the glucocorticoid class of hormones and a stress hormone.
This progressive, incurable neurocognitive syndrome — often tied to Alzheimer's — brings a decline in memory, thinking and motivation across mild-to-major stages. What is it?

Dementia is a syndrome, often associated with neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, and characterized by a general decline in cognitive processes that affects the ability to perform everyday activities.

Defined in humans as an adult height of 147 centimeters or less, this condition can be disproportionate (affecting limbs or torso alone) or proportionate, and typically comes with normal intelligence and near-normal life expectancy — which condition?
Dwarfism is a condition of people and animals marked by unusually small size or short stature.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
A Hollywood star of Algiers and Boom Town, this Austrian-American actress also co-invented a wartime radio guidance system — who was she?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 - January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.
Petroleum, natural gas, and coal all fall under which class of organic compound built solely from hydrogen and carbon, spanning gases, liquids, waxes, and polymers?
Hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.
Serving as the continuous analog of a summation, this fundamental calculus operation is used to compute areas, volumes, and displacement from velocity — name the mathematical concept?
Integral is the continuous analog of a sum, and is used to calculate areas, volumes, and their generalizations.
This American physicist revived general relativity in postwar America and had a knack for naming things — coining "quantum foam," "wormhole," and the term "black hole" itself. Who is he?
John Archibald Wheeler (July 9, 1911 - April 13, 2008) was an American theoretical physicist.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
Named for the Latin word for weighing scales and lying between Virgo and Scorpius, this faint zodiac constellation has no first-magnitude stars — which one?
Libra (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

While at IBM in the 1960s, this computer scientist invented a key technique behind the out-of-order execution most modern processors use — then was fired in 1968 for planning a gender transition, an act IBM apologized for in 2020. Who was this engineer?
Lynn Conway (January 2, 1938 - June 9, 2024) was an American computer scientist, electrical engineer, and transgender rights activist.
Among the first women in Canada to earn a medical doctorate, this physician-chemist is best remembered for a landmark 1913 enzyme-kinetics paper co-authored with Leonor Michaelis — who was she?
Maud Menten (March 20, 1879 - July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Unlike its cousin hemoglobin, this protein binds oxygen without cooperative binding and only shows up in a human's bloodstream after muscle injury — which protein?
Myoglobin (symbol Mb or MB) is an iron- and oxygen-binding protein found in the cardiac and skeletal muscle tissue of vertebrates in general and in almost all mammals.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
Atomic number 8 and a potent oxidizing agent, this element pairs up into a colorless, odorless diatomic gas and tops the list of elements in Earth's crust — what is it?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
This aromatic herb is a natural hybrid between watermint and spearmint, native to Europe and the Middle East but now cultivated worldwide — what plant is it?
Peppermint (Mentha piperita) is a hybrid species of mint, a cross between watermint and spearmint.

This roundworm is one of the most common intestinal parasites in humans, causing a condition sometimes called oxyuriasis after the family it belongs to, and has also been found in bonnet macaques — what's the parasite?
Pinworm (parasite) (species Enterobius vermicularis), also known as threadworm (in the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand) or seatworm, is a parasitic worm.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
This British economist won the 1991 Nobel Memorial Prize and warned that the field was "suicidal" to become a hard science of choice while ignoring society, history, and culture — who was he?
Ronald Coase (29 December 1910 - 2 September 2013) was a British economist and author.
Developed by the MIT Media Lab for children ages 5 to 16, this block-based visual programming language and website has been translated into more than 70 languages — name it?
Scratch (programming language) is a high-level, block-based visual programming language and website aimed primarily at children as an educational tool, with a target audience of ages 5 to 16.
Marked by reduced muscle activity yet busy, active brain patterns, this state alternates between REM and non-REM cycles — what is it?
Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited.

After more than 40 years at DuPont, this Polish-American chemist became the first woman to win the company's Lavoisier Medal — an honor that recognized her invention of a famously bullet-stopping fiber. Who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek (July 31, 1923 - June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
These large, often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae number over a thousand species, and New World pet varieties can flick irritating 'urticating hairs' at threats. What creatures are they?
Tarantula are a group of large and often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae.

Proposing an information management system in March 1989 and implementing the first successful client-server exchange that November, this English computer scientist invented HTML, HTTP and the URL system — who is he?
Tim Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955), also known as TimBL, is an English computer scientist best known as the inventor of the World Wide Web, HTML, the URL system, and HTTP.
Nicknamed carbamide, this is the simplest amide of carbamic acid: two amino groups joined by a single carbonyl, and the body's chief way of shedding nitrogen in urine. What compound is it?
Urea (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
Discovered in 1807 and named for the Roman goddess of home and hearth, this is thought to be the second-largest asteroid and the only known rocky protoplanet still intact in the belt — which one?
4 Vesta: Second largest main-belt asteroid. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Native to sub-Saharan grasslands and woodlands, this animal is the largest living land species, with the largest recorded specimen standing nearly 13 feet tall at the shoulder — which species is it?
African bush elephant: Species of mammal. Its skin is grey with scanty hairs, and bending cracks which support thermoregulation by retaining water.

Its seasonal form is called hay fever: a type I hypersensitivity reaction where the immune system overreacts to airborne allergens, bringing sneezing, a runny nose, and itchy, watery eyes — what's the medical name?
Allergic rhinitis: Nasal inflammation due to allergens in the air.
This scientific discipline uses techniques from titration to mass spectrometry to identify unknown compounds and measure exactly how much of each substance is present in a mixture - which field?
Analytical chemistry: Study of the separation, identification, and quantification of matter.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.

First catalogued in 1729 by an Italian priest who thought its spore-forming structures resembled a holy-water sprinkler, this genus of several hundred mold species takes its name from the Latin word for 'to sprinkle' — which genus?
Aspergillus: Genus of fungi. Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'heavy,' this soft silvery alkaline earth metal with atomic number 56 wasn't isolated until 1808 via electrolysis, decades after being identified — which element?
Barium: Chemical element with atomic number 56 (Ba)
Produced continuously by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, this yellow-green fluid is released into the small intestine to help digest fats — what is it?
Bile: Dark greenish-brown fluid aiding in the digestion of fats.

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Named for both the tree and its edible nut, this genus of temperate deciduous trees belongs to the beech family — what is it?
Chestnut: Genus of plants. The name also refers to the edible nuts they produce.
Homologous with the male foreskin and developing as part of the labia minora, which fold of skin surrounds and protects the tip of the clitoris?
Clitoral hood: Part of the vulva that covers and protects the glans of the clitoris.
The largest living bird species, this flightless native of Africa is one of just two living species in its genus — which bird?
Common ostrich: Species of flightless bird. The common ostrich is one of two extant species of ostriches, the only living members of the genus Struthio in the ratite group of birds.
Found mainly in muscle and brain tissue, which organic compound helps recycle ATP — its phosphorylated form donating phosphate to ADP to regenerate the body's energy currency?
Creatine: Chemical compound. Creatine ( or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
Most genera in this family of armored, burrowing mammals are extinct — only one genus survives today, with eight living species — which family?

This widely used polar aprotic solvent dissolves both polar and nonpolar compounds, mixes with water, and — once absorbed through the skin — leaves a curious garlic-like taste in the mouth. Which organosulfur compound is it?
Dimethyl sulfoxide: Organosulfur chemical compound used as a solvent.

This movement disorder causes involuntary muscle contractions that twist the body into abnormal postures, and can sometimes be treated with botulinum toxin injections or deep brain stimulation — what is it?
Dystonia: Neurological movement disorder. Dystonia is often intensified or exacerbated by physical activity, and symptoms may progress into adjacent muscles.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
This Stanford computer scientist built ImageNet, the vast labeled dataset that ignited the deep-learning revolution in computer vision in the 2010s. Who is she?
Also called vitamin B9, this essential nutrient the body can't make itself is vital for building DNA and RNA — which is why its synthetic form, folic acid, is added to fortified foods. What is it?
Folate: Vitamin B9; nutrient essential for DNA synthesis. Folate, also known as vitamin B9 and folacin, is one of the B vitamins.
Also known as reishi or lingzhi, this red-colored fungus grows on decaying hardwood in parts of Europe and China — what is it?
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).
Designed specifically for airborne early warning rather than adapted from an existing airframe, this twin-turboprop carrier plane replaced the piston-engined Tracer for the US Navy — which aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye: Airborne early warning and control aircraft. The Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)
Also called Hansen's disease, this slow bacterial infection dulls the body's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed injuries can cost a person their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy: Chronic disease caused by bacterial infection.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German physicist originated quantum theory and lent his name to a fundamental physical constant — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Robaxin and developed in 1956, this centrally acting muscle relaxant treats short-term musculoskeletal pain but its exact mechanism remains unclear — what is it?
Methocarbamol: Medication for musculoskeletal pain. It may be used together with rest, physical therapy, and pain medication.
Most under a millimeter long, these eight-legged arachnids include the parasite that plagues honeybee colonies and the species behind scabies in humans — what are they?
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
This burrowing, semiaquatic South American rodent munches river-plant stems and was shipped worldwide by fur farmers, only to become a destructive invasive pest — which animal is it?
Nutria: Semi-aquatic rodent from South America.
Farmed largely around a South African town, this flightless bird is the heaviest bird alive and can sprint 70 km/h — the fastest of any bird on land. What is it?
Ostrich: Genus of largest living birds.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

Not approved for general use in the US but sold across Europe for conditions such as vertigo and cortical myoclonus, this drug is a cyclic derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA and belongs to the 'racetam' group — what is it?
Domesticated some 7,000 to 10,000 years ago in what is now southern Peru, this starchy underground tuber belongs to the nightshade family — what is it?
Potato: Starchy tuber used as a staple food.
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

A pioneer in optical character recognition and speech synthesis, this futurist inventor received the National Medal of Technology from President Clinton in 1999 for his outlook on AI and life extension — who is he?
Ray Kurzweil: American computer scientist, author and futurist (born 1948)
Often called the first modern chemist, which 17th-century Anglo-Irish natural philosopher described the inverse relationship between a gas's pressure and volume in a law that bears his name?
Named for the genus of the Atlantic salmon, this family of cold-water fish also includes trout, char, and grayling — what family is it?
People with this anxiety disorder are fully capable of speech but fall silent in specific situations or around specific people, even when staying quiet brings shame or punishment — what is it called?
Selective mutism: Anxiety disorder blocking speech. Selective mutism usually co-exists with social anxiety disorder.
This layer of tissue covering a vertebrate's body serves three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation?
